findings.heading: Major revisions / Büyük güncellemeler
findings.proposition: Version 1.0.1 of the handbook was released on 20 Nov 2022. The English revision table carries this row; the Turkish table stops at the 10 May 2021 row for version 1.0.0.
findings.reader_consequence: A Turkish reader believes the latest handbook release is 1.0.0 from May 2021 and cannot tell which version of the text they are reading.

findings.heading: Major revisions / Büyük güncellemeler
findings.proposition: The English section carries a NEWS block listing nine substantive changes implemented in version 1.0.1 (update to R 4.2; {linelist} replaced by {matchmaker} in data cleaning; guess_date() replaced by parsedate::parse_date(); pivot_wider() id_cols= update; plot_age_pyramid() replaced by age_pyramid(); ungroup() added to the agg_weeks chunks in heat plots and interactive plots; data.frame() added around trending::fit()/predict() objects; case_when() switched to ifelse() plus optional across() code in combinations analysis; {epicontacts} updated). The Turkish section has no NEWS block at all.
findings.reader_consequence: A Turkish reader does not learn that packages and functions used elsewhere in the handbook were replaced, so they may follow retired code (for example {linelist} guess_date()) that the English edition explicitly records as superseded.

findings.heading: Editorial decisions / Editöryal Kararlar
findings.proposition: In English, 'dependability' is the stated rationale for choosing incidence2 and ggplot2 for epidemic curves, and it sits in its own rationale cell. The Turkish row has only three cells and folds the word into a claim that ggplot2 is 'detailed and dependable', so dependability becomes a property attributed to ggplot2 alone rather than the reason for the decision.
findings.reader_consequence: A Turkish reader reads the rationale column as empty for this row and infers that incidence2 is fast but not dependable, which the English text does not say.

findings.heading: Editorial decisions / Editöryal Kararlar
findings.proposition: English gives the epiweeks rationale as lubridate's flexibility, consistency, and its prospects for continued package maintenance. Turkish states that lubridate is 'flexible, consistent and an option that preserves the other packages' (diger paketleri koruyan bir secenek), which asserts something about lubridate's effect on other packages instead of about lubridate's own maintenance outlook.
findings.reader_consequence: A Turkish reader takes away a false technical property of lubridate and loses the actual selection criterion, which is whether the package will keep being maintained.

findings.heading: Editorial decisions / Editöryal Kararlar
findings.proposition: English states that str_glue() is within the stringr package. Turkish states that str_glue() 'contains stringr functions' (stringr fonksiyonlarini icerir), reversing the containment relationship between the function and the package.
findings.reader_consequence: A Turkish reader may not realise stringr is the package to install or load in order to use str_glue().

findings.heading: Editorial decisions / Editöryal Kararlar
findings.proposition: The English second column is headed 'Considered', naming every option that was weighed. The Turkish header is 'Paket' (Package), while the column's own contents include bare functions such as library(), install.packages(), require(), factor(), paste(), labs() and ggtitle().
findings.reader_consequence: A Turkish reader loses the fact that the column lists the alternatives that were evaluated, and the header is contradicted by the function names inside the column.

findings.heading: Editorial decisions / Editöryal Kararlar
findings.proposition: English gives the janitor rationale as 'Consolidation of packages emphasized', that is, keeping the number of distinct packages down. Turkish says 'Paketlerin birlikte kullanimi vurgulanmaktadir' (the joint use of packages is emphasised), which states the opposite editorial principle.
findings.reader_consequence: A Turkish reader infers the handbook favours combining more packages, when the stated policy is to reduce how many packages a task needs.
